renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: sintax_sunburst
  title: Kingdom and phylum composition
  description: |-
    Each arc is a taxon: the inner ring is the kingdom and the outer ring the phylum, sized by relative abundance summed over the samples in view and coloured by phylum. It answers which groups dominate the community.
    How to read: a wide arc is a dominant phylum, and many thin arcs a diverse community. Click an arc to zoom into it, and filter the samples to see how the composition shifts. An Unclassified arc means the reference database could not place those sequences.
    Source: https://github.com/torognes/vsearch
  kind: sunburst
  config:
    colour_by_rank: Phylum
  roles:
    ranks:
    - Kingdom
    - Phylum
    abundance: rel_abundance

- component: figure
  title: Relative abundance by phylum
  description: |-
    Each box is a phylum: the spread of its relative abundance over the samples in view. It answers which phyla carry most of the community and how much that varies.
    How to read: a few high boxes and a long tail near zero is the usual shape of an amplicon community. A wide box is a phylum whose share changes between samples; filter by kingdom or sample to see which samples drive it.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: Phylum
    y: rel_abundance
    color: Phylum
    labels:
      Phylum: Phylum
      rel_abundance: Relative abundance

- component: card
  title: Samples classified
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of samples with a classification, with the number of sample and phylum rows next to it, and the bars rank the phyla seen in the most samples. It answers how many samples the composition rests on.
    How to read: a phylum present in few samples is a sporadic taxon. The ranking shows which phyla are shared across the samples.
  column: sample
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: Phylum
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: samples, by phylum

- component: card
  title: Phyla resolved
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct named phyla found, and the bars rank the samples by how many phyla they hold. It answers how diverse the community is at phylum level.
    How to read: a sample with few phyla is dominated by one lineage. Sequences the classifier could not place are left out of the count.
  column: Phylum
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  filter_expr: col('Phylum') != 'Unclassified'
  caption: phyla, by sample
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Dominant phylum share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest relative abundance any phylum reaches in a sample, with the median and the upper quartile of all phylum shares next to it. It answers how dominated the community is by one lineage.
    How to read: a maximum close to 1 means one phylum makes up nearly a whole sample. A median far below it is the usual long tail of minor phyla.
  column: rel_abundance
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - q3
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: largest share, with the median and the upper quartile

- component: interactive
  title: Kingdom
  description: |-
    Choose one or more kingdoms to restrict the tiles of this tab to them. It answers how a single domain of life contributes to the composition.
    How to read: pick a kingdom to see only its phyla in the sunburst and the boxes.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: Kingdom

- component: interactive
  title: Phylum
  description: |-
    Choose one or more phyla to restrict the tiles of this tab to them. It answers how a single phylum is distributed across the samples.
    How to read: pick a phylum to compare its relative abundance between samples.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: Phylum

- component: table
  title: Relative abundance per sample and phylum
  description: |-
    Each row is a phylum in one sample: its taxonomy, the kingdom and the relative abundance. It answers exactly which taxa each sample holds and at what share.
    How to read: sort by relative abundance to find the dominant phylum of a sample.
